materials.name: Culture medium
materials.notes: Background. Matches the water-like peak in water_plexiglass.csv.

materials.name: Cytoplasm
materials.notes: Typical of the bulk cell body across the data/csv scans.

materials.name: Nucleus
materials.notes: Stiffer and brighter than cytoplasm; the usual segmentation target.

materials.name: Nucleolus
materials.notes: Small high-shift inclusion, useful for testing spatial resolution.

materials.name: Lipid droplet
materials.notes: Low-shift inclusion; tests whether an algorithm can resolve both signs.

materials.name: Collagen fibre
materials.notes: Stiff extracellular structure; well separated from the cell body.

materials.name: Polystyrene dish
materials.notes: Culture plate under the cells. Most Plate2/Plate3 scans in data/csv show a weak, near-uniform peak at 10.4-10.6 GHz, which is where polystyrene lands at this wavelength.

materials.name: Plexiglass (PMMA)
materials.notes: Shift measured directly from water_plexiglass.csv, where the peak at 11.75 GHz is anti-correlated with the water peak at r = -0.96.

materials.name: Glass substrate
materials.notes: Coverslip. Its Brillouin line sits far outside the +-14.9 GHz window, so it contributes elastic signal only - which is what a real coverslip does.
